correctness.rationale: The two positive information-class balances force U=u and I=i. The population totals and R balance force q, s and R, and the remaining equation is p(1+M)=1+Z with M+Z=q, hence the stated strict feasibility interval and uniqueness. For stability, in independent M,Z,I,R coordinates write Q for the linearized perturbation of M+Z. An eigenvalue in the closed right half-plane with λ≠0 gives Q=dI/(λ+a), M=−(a−c)Q/λ, Z=Q−M and R=εγI/(λ+εt); if the infected perturbation I were zero, the whole eigenvector would vanish. The resulting scalar equation has the terms λ+εf+ε²fγ/(λ+εt)+εdB(a−c)/(aλ)+εd(cB−aA)/(a(λ+a)). If the last residue is negative, the maximum fractional loss of the positive constant f is [Ks/(1−Ki)]·[uz(m−z)/(q²(1+z)(1+m))]<1/8, using z(m−z)=z(q−2z)≤q²/8 and Ks<1−Ki. Thus the real part is strictly positive even on the imaginary axis. Zero is excluded directly: the M row forces Q=0, the Z row forces I=0, the R row forces R=0 and the infected row fixes M=Z=0. The normal rates follow from the two scalar population-total equations. This establishes exponential stability for fixed ε>0 without assuming a uniform rate as ε tends to zero or any global result. The supplied exact-rational verifier and notes were inspected, not executed; the algebraic obstruction, not the finite examples, is the replay path for the universal conclusion.

value.rationale: For a published coupled ODE with a coexistence example but no general quartic classification in the inspected source, excluding local instability throughout its entire feasible time-scale family resolves a concrete mathematical gap. The feedback positivity argument also explains why a time-scale sweep alone cannot change local stability. This has value independently of the concise feasibility correction, without claiming global convergence.
